clues: This town sits at the foot of a tall range of peaks, in dry south-west land. A small river runs through it, past old adobe streets.
Most months here are dry, with cool winters and hot summers. Then the monsoon comes, and July and August bring the year's heaviest rains.
In 1610, the Spanish governor named this town the capital of his province. It has kept that role, with short breaks, ever since that year.
This town is the oldest state capital in the whole country. It is also the earliest town built by Europeans west of the great river.
Rulers of old ran New Mexico from a palace in this city. Now its laws are made here, in the state capital.
